claims.claim: Evagrius Ponticus was a Christian monk and ascetic who lived from about 345 to 399 AD, was born in Ibora in the Roman province of Pontus and died in the Nitrian Desert of Egypt.
After a personal spiritual crisis he left his ecclesiastical career, took monastic vows in Jerusalem in 383, and spent the remainder of his life in the Egyptian desert at Nitria and Kellia.
The treatise De vitiis quae opposita sunt virtutibus is addressed to the monk Eulogios, who is also the recipient of the related work CPG 2447.

In the work Evagrius briefly outlines nine pairs of vices and their opposite virtues (gluttony/abstinence, fornication/chastity, avarice/freedom from possessions, sadness/joy, anger/patience, acedia/perseverance, vainglory/freedom from vainglory, jealousy/freedom from jealousy, pride/humility).
The Greek text of De vitiis quae opposita sunt virtutibus survives in the Patrologia Graeca (Migne) edition and is available online as a PDF.
The work also survives in a Syriac translation, which has been edited and published in modern scholarly editions.
